When advertised, adf is a JSON document object; markdown and plain_text are strings converted to ADF. Format is never inferred; read this action's contentFormat enum. This comment action is absent when its native ADF target is disabled. Do not append your own attribution footer; configured attribution is applied in native ADF when content is written. Oversize content returns body_size_denied/413 and an unsupported format returns body_format_unsupported/415; source and converted content are omitted from audit and diagnostics.

issue.child.create.workflow: Create a new issue already attached to the parent named by exactly one of parentIssue or parentUrl. Discover issueTypeId with issue_type.list and pass the returned string ID unchanged. Both the target project and resolved parent project must be authorized. Jira's hierarchy and issue-type rules still apply; arbitrary custom fields are unsupported. This is independently authorized from issue.create and has no rollback with earlier or later workflow calls. Use issue.parent.set to attach an existing issue instead.

issue.create.scope: Authorization is by Jira project. Use the Jira project key, not a policy resource ID; an issue locator does not introduce a separate issue grant.
issue.create.readPresentation: When advertised, non-native readContentFormat adds a Markdown/text renderedBody to the owning issue while preserving its native ADF. It formats the returned body without an additional provider fetch; write contentFormat remains a separate control.
issue.create.content: Supply content with explicit contentFormat for the description. The pair is optional; omit both for no description. When advertised, adf is a JSON document object; markdown and plain_text are strings converted to ADF. Format is never inferred; read this action's contentFormat enum. Do not append your own attribution footer; configured attribution is applied in native ADF when content is written. issue.create.workflow: Discover issueTypeId with jira.issue_type.list using the intended credential context and pass its decimal-string ID unchanged. Only project, issueTypeId, summary and the optional content pair are writable; arbitrary custom fields are unsupported. Creating an Epic, creating children and adding dependencies are separate authorized mutations without a multi-call rollback. Use issue.child.create for a new child or issue.parent.set for an existing issue.

issue.dependency.add.workflow: blockingIssue/blockingUrl names the issue that blocks blockedIssue/blockedUrl. Give exactly one locator per side; the issues must differ and both projects must be authorized. The configured dependency link is verified in that direction by readback. This call is independently authorized and does not roll back earlier Epic/child/parent mutations.
issue.dependency.add.typedCommand: Typed CLI wrapper: agent-access jira issue dependency add [OPTIONS]; run agent-access jira issue dependency add --help for flags and input alternatives.

issue.parent.set.workflow: Assign an existing issue to exactly one parentIssue or parentUrl; select the child with issue or url. The child and parent must be distinct, and both resolved projects must be authorized. Jira decides hierarchy/issue-type compatibility. The action is independently authorized and verifies the parent by readback; it does not roll back other Epic workflow calls or accept arbitrary custom fields.
issue.parent.set.typedCommand: Typed CLI wrapper: agent-access jira issue parent set [OPTIONS] [ISSUE]; run agent-access jira issue parent set --help for flags and input alternatives.

issue.update.content: Supply content with explicit contentFormat for the description. The pair is optional when summary is supplied; give at least summary or a complete content pair. When advertised, adf is a JSON document object; markdown and plain_text are strings converted to ADF. Format is never inferred; read this action's contentFormat enum. Do not append your own attribution footer; configured attribution is applied in native ADF when content is written. issue.update.update: Updates only summary and description. Give at least summary or a complete content/contentFormat pair; omitted content leaves the description unchanged. notifyUsers is optional: omission leaves Jira's default, while true/false are sent explicitly. Jira may require additional upstream permission to suppress notifications. Returned changedFields is ordered summary then description.
issue.update.typedCommand: Typed CLI wrapper: agent-access jira issue update [OPTIONS] [ISSUE]; run agent-access jira issue update --help for flags and input alternatives.

issue.custom_field.set.scope: Authorization is by Jira project; a grant for issue.update alone does not grant this action. The operator must allow fieldId in providers.jira.custom_fields.allowed_field_ids; the default empty list permits no custom-field writes. The provider-wide allowlist applies to every caller with matching action and project authority, allowing each caller to write every listed field. Use the issue key or accepted browser URL, not a policy resource ID.
issue.custom_field.set.workflow: Set one operator-allowed custom field. Supply exactly one issue or url locator, a canonical customfield_<positive decimal ID> fieldId, and a present value of any JSON type, including null to request clearing. JSON strings are passed unchanged, never parsed again. Null issue/url locators are treated as omitted; exactly one non-null locator is required. Optional expectedIssueId is a positive decimal string that must match the resolved immutable issue ID before writing. Jira decides the field type, context, editability and requiredness; it may reject a value or null.
issue.custom_field.set.authority: Allowlisting a field delegates any value or clear that Jira accepts for that field, together with its field-specific effects. Operators must verify those effects before listing it. Configured comment/description attribution does not add attribution to custom ADF fields. The action exposes no transition, notification or override controls and preserves Jira notification defaults.
issue.custom_field.set.result: Returns operation=issue.custom_field.set, the confirmed issue identity, fieldId and status=set after one PUT containing only the selected field and addressed by the confirmed immutable issue ID. This acknowledges Jira acceptance; it does not read back or return the field value, field name or raw custom data. No current-value check or duplicate-write suppression is performed. Field values and names are omitted from audit. Accepted writes whose result cannot be completed retain the standard applied_unverified receipt, and uncertain requests are not safe to replay blindly.
issue.custom_field.set.errors: jira_custom_field_not_allowed means the operator has not allowed this field ID. jira_custom_field_rejected means Jira refused the edit with HTTP 400 or 422; no raw Jira error content is returned. These are nonretryable configuration or value errors. The serialized JSON value is bounded by content.max_body_bytes; an excess returns body_size_denied. Ordinary transport and request-body limits also apply. An expectedIssueId mismatch or an issue that has left the admitted projects returns scope_unresolved before any write and carries no mutation receipt.

issue.view.scope: Authorization is by Jira project. Use the issue key or accepted browser URL, not a policy resource ID; an issue locator does not introduce a separate issue grant.
issue.view.presentation: Whole-result Markdown omits null standard context and shows None. for empty collections. Named values keep their IDs even when names are unavailable. Custom fields use readable names and IDs with explicit unsupported/withheld markers; custom-field nulls and empty arrays display as not set. An empty customFields array means no custom fields were returned, not that the project defines none. A returned null parent displays No parent returned. Embedded formatting retains native ADF and adds renderedBody beside the owning issue, comment or supported ADF custom-field value.
issue.view.discussionPaging: With includeComments=true, continue commentPage.nextStartAt through jira.comment.list with includeBodies=true. Keep chosen list size/order settings. isLast=true establishes completion of the visible page stream; null means unknown. Pages are independently authorized and are not a snapshot; a reply's parentCommentId may refer to another page. A byte-limited page contains fewer whole comments, never shortened bodies. Omitting includeComments or setting it false needs no comment companions, and selecting a presentation format alone never fetches comments.
issue.view.resultMetadata: Issue metadata includes timestamps, small user summaries, priority and labels when Jira returns them. Detailed context, custom fields and eligible embedded references are exclusive to issue.view and are absent from search and mutation readbacks.

project.list.request: Omitting maxResults uses the configured maximum advertised by this action (50 in the default configuration, at most 100). Results contain items, count, maxResults and scanStatus; count is not an upstream total.

project.view.searchWorkflow: Use each returned jqlReference in a separately authorized search, for example cf[12345]. Do not substitute a display name or customfield_12345. Custom-field functions and sorting are unsupported; discovery does not establish creation requirements or field options.
project.view.resultPresentation: When advertised, whole-result Markdown preserves returned identifiers/timestamps as code spans and safe URLs as autolinks, neutralizes metadata controls/newlines and uses only the existing result. Selecting a format does not fetch bodies or add requests.

search.parentFilters: Use parent = PROJ-100 for direct children, or parent IN (PROJ-100, 10001) for keys and positive decimal IDs. Also supports != and NOT IN. Projects narrow children; parent references may name inaccessible projects and reveal relationships without parent lookups or parent metadata. Search permission suffices. Embedded issue.view hierarchy remains gated by effective all-project access. No parentEpic, recursion, EMPTY, functions or parent sorting. Negative parent filters alone require finite projects or an additional filter.
search.resultMetadata: Search results contain issue timestamps, small user summaries, priority and labels when supplied. They omit description bodies, detailed issue context, customFields, parent, subtasks and issueLinks. Whole-result formatting does not fetch those fields; use a separately authorized issue.view when needed.
search.fieldDiscovery: Use jira.project.view to discover a project's searchable fields and supported operators. Exclusions and text negation are advertised only when Jira reports the operator and Broker supports it. Insert the returned jqlReference such as cf[12345]; do not use the display name or customfield_12345. Text ~ and !~ use Jira text-search semantics rather than whole-value comparisons. Jira validates each custom field's configured type and searcher when searching; discovery is not a prerequisite. Field/operator combinations rejected by Jira return the existing generic upstream_failed response.
search.resultPresentation: When advertised, whole-result Markdown preserves returned identifiers/timestamps as code spans and safe URLs as autolinks, neutralizes metadata controls/newlines and uses only the existing result. Selecting a format does not fetch bodies or add requests.

verify.expectations: Give at least expectCommentId or expectAttachmentId with the issue key. Use returned comment/attachment IDs from the preceding operation. Read verification.status to distinguish matched from mismatch; verification has its own project authorization and is available as whole-result Markdown when advertised.

issue.transition.list.workflow: Discover the next transitions on this issue, then select a transitionId and its to.id for issue.transition.apply. Different projects and issue types may have different workflows. Keep list and apply grants in the same credential mode when possible; apply independently rechecks with its own selected execution credential. No workflow bypass flags are exposed.
issue.transition.list.result: Returns issue identity, currentStatus with id/name/statusCategory, and transitions with id/name/to/hasScreen. Each collection contains at most 100 entries and reports count and truncated. includeFields adds fields.items with id/name/required/hasDefaultValue/brokerInput; only resolution advertises brokerInput=resolutionId and bounded allowedValues. Other field values, defaults, URLs and arbitrary schema objects are withheld. A missing fields value is null, meaning Jira did not supply metadata. Names are limited to 1024 UTF-8 bytes, numeric IDs to 64 bytes; malformed or oversized entries fail. Each upstream response is capped at the smaller of 1 MiB and the configured upstream response limit.
issue.transition.list.requirements: The list describes Jira availability under this action's credential, not authority or guaranteed success for apply. An empty list may reflect permissions or current state. Field requirements are informative; existing values, defaults and workflow validators remain Jira-controlled. Unsupported submitted fields require a separately designed operation; apply never chains field or comment writes.
issue.transition.list.typedCommand: Typed CLI wrapper: agent-access jira issue transition list [OPTIONS] [ISSUE]; run agent-access jira issue transition list --help for flags and input alternatives.
issue.transition.list.scope: Authorization is by Jira project. Use an issue key or accepted browser URL; the current project is resolved and reconfirmed through issue metadata.

issue.transition.apply.workflow: Apply exactly one transitionId discovered for this issue and its toStatusId. The issue is resolved for project authorization and reconfirmed; current status and selected transition are checked with the execution credential, and the POST targets the confirmed immutable issue ID. expectedIssueId and expectedStatusId are optional pre-send guards. Destination/current-state checks are not atomic with the POST and cannot establish safe replay.
issue.transition.apply.fields: Only optional resolutionId is submitted as fields.resolution.id. No custom fields, comments, descriptions, arbitrary fields/update, history metadata, properties or notification controls are accepted. Jira validates resolution and other workflow requirements. The action delegates the selected workflow transition, including Jira-controlled post-functions, automation and notifications. Existing issue-edit or custom-field grants do not grant this action.
issue.transition.apply.result: Jira acceptance returns status=transitioned and transitionId/fromStatusId/toStatusId. A compact readback yields verification.status=matched or differs and verification.observedStatus. A difference is a successful observation, not a failed mutation; neither value proves this request caused the observed state. If the readback fails, the error carries applied_unverified with post_transition_readback. A timeout, disconnect or ambiguous upstream failure may leave an unknown outcome; never automatically replay. The ordinary one-time Atlassian OAuth 401 renewal remains supported.
issue.transition.apply.errors: jira_transition_unavailable means the transition or expected state/destination did not match before sending. jira_transition_rejected means Jira rejected the submitted transition; check permissions, workflow requirements and resolution. Errors do not enumerate other transitions or expose raw Jira validation messages. A read-only caller cannot apply transitions. List and apply grants are independent and can select different credentials; discovery is advisory.
issue.transition.apply.typedCommand: Typed CLI wrapper: agent-access jira issue transition apply [OPTIONS] --transition-id <TRANSITION_ID> --to-status-id <TO_STATUS_ID> [ISSUE]; run agent-access jira issue transition apply --help for flags and input alternatives.
